amendments.reason: A local harness preview (Mac, ROS 2 Humble, not the Foxy target, not evidence) showed both builds ending about 8 cm from the target after follow-up replans (original 0.0785 m, candidate 0.0805 m; single-call candidate at most 0.0437 m). Follow-up calls accept through the previous-trajectory branch, which the one-line fix does not touch. All 8 accepted trajectories inside the inflated near box were original-build trajectories (candidate 0).
amendments.unchanged: acceleration gate 1.5 m/s^2, single-call endpoint limit 0.05 m, zero collision samples, AC0, AC2, AC5, AC6

changes: AC3 follow-up endpoints are reported, not judged; the D8 per-call rule is removed
amendments.reason: The D8 per-call pairing is not meaningful: after call 0 the two builds' trajectories diverge, so call i of each build starts from a different state. Call 0 is already judged by the single-call rule, where the fix's known endpoint shift is 1-2.5 cm. The same local Humble preview (not evidence) had 7 follow-up calls over original + 0.01 m: call 0 shifts of 1.0-1.3 cm, and call 1 at x = -1.09 and -1.10 m ended 0.001 and 0.005 m from the target in the original but 0.077 and 0.081 m in the candidate. Follow-up completion stays judged by AC6; final position is judged by the Isaac arrival checks (AC7).
amendments.unchanged: single-call endpoint limit 0.05 m, AC0, AC2, AC4 (D8 form), AC5, AC6

sampled_max_acc_method: norm of the second derivative of the returned position spline at 1001 uniform samples, as diagnosticSpline in scan_replan_diagnosis/instrument_manager.py
endpoint_xy_derivation: D7; derived from the 0.25 m arrival tolerance, fixed before the candidate was run on new fixtures
endpoint_method: XY distance from the returned spline position at its full duration to the target passed to that call
collision_method: scan_replan_fsm.cpp checkCollisionCallback loop from t=0: every 0.01 s, GridMap::getInflateOccupancy(pos, yaw of the next 0.01 s segment); any nonzero value (inflated occupied = 1, outside the map = -1) counts

follow_up.timing_method: requested and measured offsets (node clock minus stored trajectory start) must equal the fixture offset differences

comparison.same_run: original and candidate runs are paired by fixture label (same start, target, map, initialization, seed and repeat)
comparison.acceptance_of_first_call: a single run is accepted when its first reboundReplan call returns true

ac0.prd: Validity control (added 2026-09-17, stricter only): the original build must reproduce the recorded failure. For failed_run_resume (polynomial, seed 0, empty map) all 3 repeats are rejected by the acceleration gate, and the other 3 recorded cases pass 3/3 each, as in native_original_20260916T180500Z. Otherwise the suite is invalid and no other native verdict is used.
ac0.on_failure: the suite is INVALID: AC2-AC6 are reported as not_evaluated and the suite does not pass

ac2.prd: The candidate returns a trajectory in every fixture where the original does, plus every acceleration-gate rejection case; every accepted trajectory's sampled maximum acceleration is at most 1.5 m/s^2.
ac2.sampled_limit_applies_to: every accepted candidate call in the whole suite; original values are reported only

ac3.prd: Native endpoint (amended 2026-09-17, D8 then D10): every accepted candidate single-call trajectory ends within 0.05 m of its target (XY). Follow-up replan endpoints of both builds are reported, not judged; follow-up completion is judged by AC6 and final position by the Isaac arrival checks (AC7).

single_call.fail_when: an accepted candidate call has endpoint_xy_m > endpoint_xy_limit_m (0.05 m)

follow_up.report: per sequence: which builds completed it, and for each call index (0, 1, 2) the endpoint_xy_m of the accepted attempt in each build (null when not accepted)

ac3.original_values: reported for every call; never judged

ac4.prd: Native, occupancy grid (amended 2026-09-17, D8): no accepted candidate trajectory has a sample inside an inflated occupied cell. Original-build hits are reported as a separate finding. Candidate rejections are reported, and count against the fix only when the original accepts the same case without a hit.
ac4.fail_when: an accepted candidate call has collision samples (inflated occupied or outside the map), or the candidate rejects a run (same label) that the original accepts with zero collision samples
ac4.findings: accepted original-build calls with collision samples are reported under findings with case, initialization, first_collision_t and duration; they do not decide AC4
ac4.not_counted: candidate rejections where the original accepted the same run only with collision samples are reported, not counted

ac5.prd: The candidate's success count is at least the original's in every case group, and any candidate-only failure is explained before continuing.
ac5.needs_explanation_when: any run the original accepts and the candidate rejects, even if the group counts pass

ac6.prd: The candidate completes every sequence the original completes, and every sequence the original fails only at the acceleration gate.
ac6.completed: the first call and every follow-up step return a trajectory (any attempt of the FSM chain)
ac6.original_fails_only_at_gate: the original does not complete and every rejected attempt in its sequence was an acceleration-gate rejection
